Testing the wording itself would take one coverage definition, re-run on a refreshed rule set with repeated seeds and scored against a reviewed human-code baseline, as G4-F136 did for the July rules. That would show whether the high coverage is over-aggression or real discrimination, and whether rule age biases comparisons across model generations.

The case for leaving the first pass alone (D01-B) is mostly right. Both new cards come from one livestream aside (2026-01-16) and are graded anecdotal ("Rule of thumb, no data"; "Minor aside"). That is the same kind of evidence the first pass already discounted, so it adds no measurement.

In the Anthropic usage block, input_tokens excludes cached tokens, and the prompt total also includes cache_creation_input_tokens. For the peak (a), the undercount is usually small, about one call's growth (§6 measured ~8-11k per call). For the decision positions (b), which decide the adopt branch, it can be large. After a cache expiry, for example while Fable waits on a long workflow before gating or judging, the whole prefix is billed as cache_creation, so a decision made at high fill reads as near zero. D01-A's autocompact-point clause holds up against a harness fact. HARNESS-REVIEW §1 Q6 and §6 lines 318-319 record the owner's autoCompactWindow of 400000, keyed to claude-opus-5-5 only. It also records the main-session model id and the autoCompactWindow in force.

Decision rules:

No percentage is cited anywhere without this counting method. Reviewer-found code defects are not used as an outcome.

The trial would then add an optional pytest-target argument for iteration runs, with the unmodified full recipe still mandatory at close.
reason: Refuted: the full gates at close already exist, the stop-hook failure behind C1255 has no counterpart in a hook-less, one-phase-per-session harness, and with python running only in Docker the per-run setup cost does not shrink with a test subset.
